$J0L0Recipient: Senior Officer of the IPSF Commandant's Office, Chornobyl Perimeter
Sender: Private Serhiy Pylypchuk
Topic: Refutation of the previous report

Dear officer,

I would like to inform you that my previous report is not true. After a detailed analysis of the situation, I realized that I had misjudged the situation in the unit and made premature conclusions.

Any conflicts or misunderstandings that may have occurred are part of normal military life and do not require intervention by the command. In fact, relations between soldiers are friendly and built on mutual respect. Older comrades always support younger ones, help them adapt to the service and pass on their invaluable experience.

I apologize for any inconvenience caused and assure you that there will be no more such misunderstandings. From now on, I will make every effort to ensure that the service is conducted flawlessly and in the proper order.

Respectfully,

Private Pylypchuk

A faint fingerprint is visible in the corner of the letter, and the last lines have barely noticeable blood-like stains.

$J0L0Hornet: Do you, Freedomers, really believe in fables about art modification?
You: These are not fables, Hornet. It's just that not everyone has access to this knowledge. You understand how the Zone works - it hides its secrets.
Hornet: Secrets or not, your experiments can lead to disaster. Did you hear about the stalker who tried to fuse the Jellyfish in a fire anomaly? There was nothing left to bury of him, and the blast was so powerful that his partners will have burns for life.
You: And another guy from our group managed to get a thing that he now hardly feels the effects of emissions. So what do you think?
Hornet: I would say that such things should not be allowed to be widely available. If some gang learns to produce such things, what then?
You: And what if this is the key to understanding the Zone? As always, Duty is afraid of change.
Hornet: Not change, but chaos.

You: Dude, where do I get this kind of money? I haven't even gotten to the proper gear yet...
[Encrypted user]: Don't talk nonsense. I don't care where you get it. Borrow it, steal it, sell it, whatever, or even kill someone. Or I'll tell everyone here that you're a snitch, and we'll see how many seconds you'll survive after the loners find out who killed their guide recently.

$J0L0You: So, Eagle, are we going or not?

sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerSkelyaControler: Messages found on a dead loner's PDA

$J0L0You: Bro, where are you? I thought you'd been killed.
You: Hellooo, Earth to Skelya. What, you got drunk on the profit you made selling those artifacts?
Skelya: I'm here.
You: Shit, finally. You're alive? Listen, you went with Hatchet and his group, right? Where were you all?!
Skelya: We were. They are no longer alive.
Skelya: We ran into trouble.
You: What trouble?
Skelya: Controller.
You: Fuck. Listen, where are you now?
Skelya: I don't know. I was walking. I was just walking. A long time. The time is mixed up. I found a rest stop, it's a little dry here.
You: Are you wounded?
Skelya: No. The body is intact. The head is not.
You: Bro, hang in there. Tell me how it happened, if you can.
Skelya: We found an anomaly. A large field, many artifacts. Hatchet was overjoyed. So was I.
You: And then what?
Skelya: We did not hear him. At first. He was somewhere there, somewhere behind us. Then his voice. It stuck in my head like a rusty knife.
You: Controller?
Skelya: Yeah. Hatchet first. He screamed. Then Woloski. They started shooting. At someone, at something.
You: Did you get hit?
Skelya: They hit each other.
You: Fuck.
Skelya: I ran away. I had a grenade, I could have thrown it... But I ran. I heard them screaming. How they were begging. How their brains were fucking melting with every second.
You: Brother, don't blame yourself...
Skelya: I left them there. I left them there. Like a cowardly asshole, you know?
You: Listen, where are you now? Tell me and I'll get you out.
Skelya: I don't know. The woods. Dark. Wet.
You: Listen, drop me a tag now. Are you still near the Yaniv Bridge?
Skelya: I don't know.I can't see it.
You: Okay, listen to me carefully.Do you have your compass with you?
Skelya: I think so.
You: Go south. If you see an old railroad car, you're on the right track. There's an old hideout not far from the station. I'll send some people.
Skelya: No.
You: The fuck you mean, no?
Skelya: I'm not going back.
You: What the fuck?
Skelya: He is still here. I can feel him. It's following me. It won't let go. I can't escape.
You: No, fuck, it's your head playing tricks on you. Wake up, motherfucker. You need to get out of here!
Skelya: He did not die. We did not kill him.
You: Forget it, just go quickly to the stash.
Skelya: I can't. But maybe I can kill him.
[Skelya user no longer online].
You: Fucking connection. Skelya, when you read this, go to the hideout, because I'll kill you myself, you fucking hero wannabe.
[Skelya user tag request sent]
You: I hope you're on your way there now, you hear?
[Request denied]
You: Answer me, fucking hell, Skelya! FUCKING ANSWER ME PLEASE, BROTHER!!!

$J0L0You: Listen, Kucher, why doesn't anyone use cars in the Zone? Seriously. There are roads.
Kucher: Have you ever seen the roads here, kid?
You: Well... I did.
Kucher: What kind of roads are these? These are pieces of asphalt between sinkholes, weeds, and anomalies.
You: Well, there must be some way to get around, right?
Kucher: Uh-huh. And now imagine that you're on a bumpy ride into an anomalous zone. Somewhere under the wheels is a Whirligig, somewhere nearby is a Burner, and you're going 80 km/h. Do you have time to slow down?
You: Well... Maybe if you know the route?
Kucher: A route? Do you think anomalies stand in place like pillars? They are constantly changing. Today, the road is clear, and tomorrow, the Electra there is so strong that you'll be reduced to coal.
You: Damn... Okay, but what if you only drive on old roads?
Kucher: Yeah, go ahead. And wait until some boar rolls you over with the car.
You: Boar?
Kucher: Boar. And not only that. The local wildlife has seen what cars are. And it has already learned how to turn them over, punch them and tear them open like a tin can.
You: What about armored vehicles?
Kucher: And if you're in it, then you're either an IPSF soldier or some moneybags so rich that they'll track you down and take it all away in three seconds.
You: Shit…
Kucher: Well, there is one more reason. Although it's so in your face that you have to have your eyes closed to not notice it yourself.
You: Just say it already.
Kucher: Fuel.
You: Yeah, what's with it?
Kucher: Nothing. It's gone. There are no gas stations in the Zone. And what is lying around in old tanks is shit, not gasoline anymore. If you put it in the tank, the engine will die.
You: For real?
Kucher: I'm telling you, it's not an option to drive around in a car. Don't even think about it.
You: I see. Very well, it's safer with my feet, either way.
Kucher: So there you have it, rookie. Just watch your surroundings, because you only have two of those.

$J0L0Cutter: So, are you alive?
You: Alive. I think.
Cutter: That's good. Because, frankly, getting you out of that shit was a real challenge.
You: I know... Thank you, brother.
Cutter: Uh-huh. But the question is, why the hell did you get into that shit?
You: I thought I'd slip through. There was an artifact there, I saw it, almost got it...
Cutter: Yeah. And then you started to twist so badly that you couldn't even call for help. Been there, seen that.
You: I remember... in fragments.
Cutter: It's good that at least I remember everything. Because, brother, I have a missing finger, and my Grom is also lost.
You: Fuck... Dude...
Cutter: Well, Grom, fuck it, even though it was a personal for me. But the finger... I could still use it, you know?
You: Dude, I don't know how to thank you.
Cutter: That's correct. How?
You: Listen... I owe you. A lot.
Cutter: Yes, and that's a significant deal.
You: Tell me what you need, and I'll do it.
Cutter: Well, you can't grow my finger back, and you can't give me back my gun, so at least let's do this: the next good artifact you find is mine.
You: Deal.
Cutter: One mroe thing.
You: Yeah?
Cutter: Don't mess with the fucking anomaly again if you don't know how it works!
You: Fuck, I get it already!
Cutter: That's good. Because I don't have the spare fingers to drag you out of that shit anymore.

sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerJokeContestI_bo:
$J0L0Boar: Well, brother, I'm sitting in my hiding place, mowed down a lot of food, and now I'm bored. Do you want to talk?
You: Of course not! I'm here in the parking lot, at Duty's, things are stale, even the thugs are not picking at it.
Boar: Well, then, let's do it this way: whoever tells the best joke is the winner and gets a box of canned food.
You: Perfect! Go ahead.
Boar: Well, listen.
A stalker is walking through the Zone, sees a Burner with an artifact in it. Well, he thinks, I'll pick it up carefully... He throws a bolt, it's fine, he walks around, stretches out his hand... Then suddenly someone behind him slaps him on the shoulder and says:
- You scared, brother?
The guy turns crimson like a tomato and screams, noticing the experienced stalker behind him:
- Are you crazy to scare me like that? What if I fell in?
The experienced guy smiles and says:
- You should be thanking me! I gave you a clue. If my joke burnt your ass so badly, the anomaly will definitely take you for one of its own, so go ahead, don't be afraid!
You: AHAHAHAHA, good one! Here, check mine:
They ask Sydorovych:
- Why do you set such high prices?
Sidor answers:
- Because I have special positions for stalkers!
- What kind?
- On their knees, with their hand outstretched...
Boar: Ahaha, that's a good one! It's a little sad, though. Hey, have you heard this one?
Two stalkers are walking through the forest at night. It's dark and creepy. One asks:
- Listen, are you afraid?
The second responds:
- Nope.
- So am I.
And from the bushes a controller watches over them and says:

You: Shit, I can't think of anything.
Boar: All right, I'll give you a one-point lead. All right, here goes one more.
A novice approaches an old stalker and asks:
- How can I survive in the Zone?
The stalker thought about it, and then he says:
- Do you see that anomaly over there?
- Where? I don't see it.
- Thats the point. Until you learn to see it, consider yourself a dead man already.
You: Fuck, this is a real thing! Yeah, listen, I remembered, but it's my last one, because my stomach hurts from laughing:
The stalker who survived the emission sits in a bar and tells the novices:
- It was so scary! The sky turned red, the earth shook! Some strange things started flashing in the air! No human could have survived that.
He is interrupted by the bartender:
- And you survived. You are a very unique person, you know. He had to get drunk with the Freedom members, break into Duty's barracks drunk, and get off only with a couple of blows with the butt of their guns and a slap on the wrist.
Boar: LMAO! You should have left that parking lot with such jokes! Bro, for this one, I'll give you a box of canned food. Come to the Bar sometime and I'll give it away.
sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerWardPastI_hint: Messages found on a dead loner's PDA
sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerWardPastI_body:
$J0L0Bug: Listen, how do you feel about the Ward? They don't seem to be that favored here.
You: Oh, here we go... So, kid, you're all for order and law in the Zone now?
Bug: They seem to keep everything under control, don't let the bandits run amok, help...
You: Ahahaha! Oh, brother, you made me laugh... The Ward? Helping people? Did you hear it from them or did some novice tell you that fairy tale?
Bug: Well, I just saw them dealing with some bandits. Not far from here.
You: Listen carefully, kid. I'm telling you once, because I don't want any problems. I've been here longer than you've been breathing, and I can tell you something about your “heroes”.
Bug: I'm all ears.
You: It was somewhere... who the fuck cares? The Ward was not the same then as now, that's the main thing. Now they pretend that they are here to improve the situation, to save everyone. But before, they were torturers.
Bug: What do you mean, torturers?
You: The torturers remain the same, even in Pripyat, too. Their first big “operation” was against free stalkers. Because we were the easiest to fucking break, in groups. Do you know what happened then?
Bug: What?
You: Their leader decided that all the free stalkers were either smugglers or potential bandits. They were ordered to “clean up” the territory and take control of everyone.
Bug: But... not everyone was lumped together like that, right?
You: Did they think long and hard, you mean? At night, they would enter stalker camps, bring everyone to their knees, and beat out confessions of “illegal activity.” And whoever could not say anything interesting was simply sent for “interrogation”. From which no one returned.
Bug: Fuck.
You: Yeah. I was at Yantar at the time. I remember one stalker, Vasya Torchok. He helped everyone, pulled people out of anomalies so many times, had a first aid kit for everyone... They took him first. Because they found a couple of rare artifacts on him.
Bug: And what happened to him?
You: They took him away. A week later he was found in swamps ten kilometers away. His legs were broken, no eyes. A real fucking stalker, gone, you know?
Bug: …
You: They set fire to hideouts, extorted bribes, and shot those who did not want to live by their rules and agreements. They didn't care, because after them, the land might as well be scorched.
Bug: But it's not like that now. Everything has changed and they are keeping things in order.
You: Fuck, they can piss in your eyes, wherever they want, and you'll still ask for more. Now they've just come up with other methods, you know? Because they realized that they have made enemies everywhere. They pretend to protect us all, that without them everything will go to hell. But if they don't like you, you're finished. Very quick and most likely in a very unpleasant way.
Bug: Fuck, I didn't know that.
You: Because you are young and naive. But if you survive in the Zone, you will know. And if you want to survive, keep your mouth shut about what was said here, and think about everything you heard before going to bed.
sid_notes_DSNoteRandMercContractI_hint: Messages found on the PDA of a dead mercenary
sid_notes_DSNoteRandMercContractI_body:
$J0L0Raven: So, how’s your latest contract?
You: Done. Not without problems, but it’s done.
Raven: What happened?
You: The target wasn’t some clueless rookie. He was holed up in a deep hideout, traps all around, plus some stalkers hanging with him. Had to wait a whole day for him to come out on his own.
Raven: You took him by wearing him out in an ambush?
You: Yup. Just watched until he exposed himself. Late at night he finally went out for a stroll — and that was it. Quiet, clean, no witnesses.
Raven: And who was he?
You: A stalker. Paranoid, hiding from everyone, but he didn’t know I was the real threat.
Raven: Harsh. Well, you ready for a new job?
You: What’s the job?
Raven: Two options.
You: Lay it on me.
Raven: The first contract is classic. There’s a stalker who knows too much. The client wants him gone. Quietly, no extra noise.
You: Tough target?
Raven: Experienced, but no bodyguards. Just cunning as a fox.
You: Location?
Raven: Roughly the eastern side of the Garbage, the place once called Dark Valley. He often hangs near an abandoned cowshed.
You: Payment?
Raven: Twenty-five thousand.
You: Huh. What about the second option?
Raven: The second one’s more interesting. There’s this self-proclaimed dealer from outside the Zone who’s been running some shady business for a while, then showing up here. Our clients want to know what he’s moving, to whom, and why.
You: So, not to take him out, but to get information out of him?
Raven: Exactly. You’d have to track him, learn his route, documents, contacts.
You: That’s trickier.
Raven: Yeah. But the pay is forty.
You: Where is he now?
Raven: He should be heading back from the Perimeter toward Wild Island in about two days.
You: So not much time.
Raven: Right.
You: If I pick one, will you give the other to someone else?
Raven: You know the rules. Choose.
You: The second.
Raven: Why?
You: Guess I’m curious. I don’t learn from others’ mistakes, apparently. Want to see what this guy is smuggling.
Raven: Alright. I’ll have the info for you in half an hour. Be ready.
sid_notes_DSNoteRandBanditKulakArmyConfl: Messages found on the PDA of a dead bandit

$J0L0You: Boss, things are totally messed up here.
Fist: Quit whining. Speak clearly.
You: The military has completely lost it lately.
Fist: Specify, what’s not clear?
You: Well, basically, we had a “route” through their checkpoints, right?
Fist: Had? Still do. So what?
You: Over the last week, they’ve literally stripped three of our guys. Just on the spot: took their cash, guns — everything.
Fist: You’re not bullshitting me? That’s a serious claim.
You: I swear. The Kozyr guys said the military even got medals for neutralizing “bandits.”
Fist: Dammit. We had a deal with their checkpoint commander. Means they’re off the leash, their word is worthless. We gotta teach ’em a lesson.
You: So what do we do?
Fist: We pull down our pants and walk around, obviously. Nah, we gotta give them a clear sign. We’ll ambush them. And do it nicely. We’ll go in at night, when they’re asleep. We’ll wipe them all out, take their guns — let them know they can’t break a deal with our crew.
You: Fist, isn’t that too big a risk? Going up against the army like that?
Fist: You scared? Or you doubting my call?
You: No!
Fist: Good. Get the guys ready, grab your guns and a couple of grenades in case those punks fight back. We meet tomorrow at our spot.

sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerArtifactEnvyI_b:
$J0L0Mazik: Bro, guess what, I FOUND an artifact MYSELF!
You: Yeah, congrats... damn it...
Mazik: You don’t get it! I found it on my own! No hints, no leads! Just walked near the bridge, saw a glimmer, tossed a bolt — and there it was!
You: Wow, what a hero... So what artifact is it?
Mazik: “Moonlight”! It glows like a flashlight and the coolest part — it seems to have zero radiation!
You: Son of a...
Mazik: Why’re you like that? Shouldn’t you be happy for me?
You: Happy? You serious? I’ve been crawling through bushes for three days, eating irradiated sausage and stale crackers, sleeping in filth, and what do I get? NOTHING!
Mazik: Well, shit happens man...
You: Meanwhile, you waltz out on your first try and bam — you got an artifact! And a damn good one!
Mazik: Hey, don’t be upset. Want to borrow it for a bit?
You: Go to hell.
Mazik: Don’t sulk, man! I know you’ve had no luck, but your time will come too.
You: Yeah, I’m starting to doubt it.
Mazik: Listen… Maybe we’ll go out together next time? I’ll share some tips!
You: “Share,” right. You gonna split if we find another artifact?
Mazik: Well... If there are two, maybe I’ll share.
You: Uh-huh. We’ll see once we actually find something.
sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerQuestionSwampsI: Messages found on a dead loner's PDA

$J0L0You: Hey, Horobets, why is there no one in the Swamps?
Horobets: Ha... Are you really that clueless, or pretending?
You: I’m serious! I heard there used to be bases there, people roaming around. Now it’s empty.
Horobets: Because those Swamps are a death trap, that’s why.
You: A death trap? Care to elaborate?
Horobets: Elaborate? Alright, listen up. Long time ago, people actually lived there. Clear Sky, free stalkers, even bandits hung around. Some were looking for artifacts, some were extorting bribes, some were just lying low to avoid the army.
You: So what happened?
Horobets: A whole lot of crap. Starting with what went down at Clear Sky’s base, ending with the Swamps basically swallowing everyone in the end.
You: Are you speaking figuratively or...?
Horobets: No, literally. There’s barely any solid ground left. One careless step and you sink into the mire. You can scream, flail your arms — still going under.
You: But there must be some dry spots?
Horobets: There used to be. Now they’re flooded too. The Zone doesn’t stand still, everything shifts, changes. Old paths went underwater, and no one’s charting new ones, because there’s nobody left to do it.
You: So it’s just swamp sludge?
Horobets: Not just that. If somehow you don’t drown, surprise — anomalies. More of them than anywhere else. And the worst part? They’re invisible.
You: How so?
Horobets: An anomaly might be right under the water. You toss a bolt — it shows nothing because there’s water on top. You step in, and that’s your will done.
You: That sounds bad.
Horobets: Think that’s all? There’s one more catch.
You: There’s more?
Horobets: No caches, no supplies left. Or if something is hidden, only its owner knows where, or maybe in a hundred years some random fool finds it by accident. You can go, waste a ton of time, risk your life — and come back with nothing.
You: What about artifacts?
Horobets: Sure, artifacts exist everywhere, but good luck getting them there among mutants, swamps, anomalies, who knows what else… Even in more familiar zones you can wind up dead chasing them, so imagine that place.
You: So basically nobody goes there anymore?
Horobets: Nobody. Because there’s no point. The Swamps just... kill you. Quietly. With no witnesses.
You: Damn, I was thinking of visiting...
Horobets: If your life doesn’t matter to you, be my guest. But I wouldn’t even look in that direction.

sid_notes_DSNoteRandFreedomFailedRaidI_b:
$J0L0Sivy: What the hell did you do?!
You: Hey, cut the attitude, Sivy. What’s wrong now?
Sivy: What’s wrong?! You led people on a raid WITHOUT the commander’s permission, and came back with no loot and two wounded!
You: We thought it would be easier to clear them out.
Sivy: “We thought”? You guys didn’t even do proper recon! Do you realize your stupidity almost cost us our men?!
You: Why are you so pissed? It’s not like I wanted our guys hurt!
Sivy: I don’t care what you wanted! The fact is, because of your “brilliant” decisions, two of ours are in the infirmary, and you brought back nothing!
You: Nothing? We at least lobbed a few grenades at those losers!
Sivy: Yeah, you chucked some grenades. So fucking what? Did you seize territory? Broke through their checkpoint?
You: …
Sivy: EXACTLY! You just rushed in, fucked up our gear, messed up the plans, and got our guys hurt!
You: Enough already. The commander tore me a new one anyway.
Sivy: You thought you’d get a commendation or something?
You: Shut it. I know I messed up!
Sivy: No, you don’t! If you did, you’d have thought before you jumped in where you shouldn’t!
You: Fine, I made a mistake! What now, a tribunal like Duty would do?
Sivy: If it were up to me, you’d be scrubbing the shitters in the bar right now.
You: Screw you!
sid_notes_DSNoteRandDutyScientistEscortI: Messages found on the PDA of a dead Duty member

$J0L0Hrim: Are you fucking serious, damn it?!
You: What now?
Hrim: Do you have any idea what in the fuck you did?!
You: You mean that egghead?
Hrim: Yeah, that damn professor we were supposed to escort! You nearly killed him, idiot! I barely covered it all up!
You: He should be grateful he’s alive. He set us up! He almost attracted mutants with his panic!
Hrim: “Set us up”? He was just doing his job and got scared! He’s a fucking civilian, not a soldier, not a stalker! They’re ALL like that, what did you expect?!
You: I don’t care who he is! He could’ve gotten us all killed if I hadn’t shut him up!
Hrim: “Shut him up”?! If you’d gone any further, you’d have put him in the ground! We’re under contract, damn it! They pay us for this shit! They PAY us for their lives!
You: Let them pay, I don’t care! I won’t let my own guys get killed because of some coward in a lab coat!
Hrim: You’ve lost your damn mind?! If we lose the trust of the fucking SIIRCA as well, we’re toast! They’ll stop providing resources, ammo! Even those few fucking scraps we get now would vanish! Our job is to protect them, not terrorize them! You want to kill civilians? Go join the bandits, they’d love you!
You: Who are you calling a bandit, you old rat?!
Hrim: You, because you think like them! No brains, no strategy! You just wanted to be done with him, right? Well, now he’s more afraid of us than of the mutants!
You: Good, let him be scared. I have no patience for him!
Hrim: I’m out of fucking patience with you too, degenerate! I’m filing a report so you’ll never escort a scientist again!
You: Shove your report, Hrim! Better yet, I’ll come find you and cram it down your ass!
sid_notes_DSNoteRandFreedomTaimedDogI_hi: Messages found on the PDA of a dead Freedom member
sid_notes_DSNoteRandFreedomTaimedDogI_bo:
$J0L0Druid: Dude, I found myself a new partner!
You: Yeah, who’d you rope into your schemes this time?
Druid: Not who, what! A blind dog!
You: … Are you fucking serious?
Druid: What’s wrong? He’s still small, not too aggressive, a bit wild, but he doesn’t bite. I think I can tame him.
You: Do you have a brain? That’s not a normal dog, it’s a mutant!
Druid: Well, all dogs were once wild before they were domesticated, right?
You: Dude, you’re either stupid or have a death wish.
Druid: Nah, man, seriously! I fed him, he didn’t growl, even wagged his tail a bit. I think if I treat him right, he can become a guard dog.
You: A guard dog… that might go nuts during an Emission!
Druid: Well, an Emission could fry my brain too. No difference, right?
You: The difference is you have a helmet and at least some brains, and that dog’s basically walking mutant bait.
Druid: You’ve seen those dogs near Rostok, right? The ones that hang around stalkers.
You: So what? They just scavenge leftover food in it's outskirts!
Druid: Exactly, and mine is already more friendly. Give it time.
You: Buddy, I can jsut about fucking picture it: we’re at the base, eating. You’re petting your freak, everything’s fine… Then something snaps in its head, and it tears your throat out.
Druid: It won’t tear my throat out.
You: How do you know?
Druid: Because I named him Bim.
You: …
Druid: Like in that book! “White Bim Black Ear”!
You: You’ve fucking absolutely lost your mind.
Druid: You just don’t understand! This is a chance! If I can actually tame him, it means not all mutants are hopeless!
You: Right. And how exactly will you craft a muzzle strong enough for him? And how will you explain he shouldn’t fucking CHEW on friendly stalkers?
Druid: He’ll figure it out on his own.
You: Right, gotcha. Good luck with your Bim, man. Just don’t let Duty see you with it.
sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerYanivTripI_hint: Messages found on a dead loner's PDA
sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerYanivTripI_body:
$J0L0Kartuz: So, bro, are you sure you’re ready for this route?
You: Man, I was fucking born ready! You doubt me?
Kartuz: Nah, just asking because it’s a long journey. From the Cordon to Yaniv isn’t like a stroll around the Bar.
You: I know, I’m not new here.
Kartuz: Alright then. The plan: we set off at dawn so we don’t run into nighttime mutants. We’ll go through the Garbage, the Bar, the Red Forest, and straight to Yanov.
You: Maybe skip the Forest? Heard that recently punks have been getting bold there again.
Kartuz: Then what do you suggest?
You: We could try Wild Territory to Yantar and skirt around, but that’s a detour, and mutants aren’t any nicer there.
Kartuz: Exactly. Through the Forest might be faster, if we move carefully.
You: Fine, you have a point.
Kartuz: Gear check. What do you have?
You: AKS-74, three mags, a shotgun with some shells. Armor’s old but still holds.
Kartuz: Medkits, anti-rad?
You: Got some, but not a lot.
Kartuz: We’ll buy more at the Bar.
You: What about food?
Kartuz: Two cans of stew and a flask of water. Enough for you?
You: If we stock up at the Bar, sure.
Kartuz: Good. As for sleeping, either at the Bar or, if we push it, somewhere between the Forest and Yaniv.
You: Let’s avoid sleeping out in the open near mutants, that’s the last thing we need...
Kartuz: True. Main thing is to get through the Forest quickly and stay out of trouble.
You: If something happens, we’ll just run, right?
Kartuz: If something happens, we’ll shoot back.
You: Right, that goes without saying.
Kartuz: Alright, get some rest. Tomorrow’s going to be a long day.
You: Roger that. At sunrise we’re hitting the road.
sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerYantarBlowoutI_: Messages found on a dead loner's PDA

$J0L0You: Dude, you alive?! Where are you?!
Shyp: Alive. Barely.
You: Where were you guys? You left in the morning, I thought you’d be at the Bar by now!
Shyp: We were returning from Yantar... and then the Blowout started.
You: Damn...
Shyp: We ran as fast as we could. There was a shelter nearby.
You: So, what happened?
Shyp: Zmiy was the first to go down. He ran ahead, and there was the damned gravsphere anomaly. One moment — gone. Just a crack-like sound, blood everywhere.
You: Fuck... What about Kriuk? Is he with you?
Shyp: Kriuk was behind. Twisted his ankle. I ran back to help him, but we had almost no time left.
You: Then what?
Shyp: He couldn’t move! He told me to drag him, but I didn’t even have a spare second.
You: ...
Shyp: I left him.
Shyp: I couldn’t do anything! Another second and I’d have died with him!
Shyp: I made it to a hideout. Locked it. Outside, everything roared and rumbled... then silence.
You: ...And?
Shyp: I went out. Kriuk was gone. Just his rifle and scraps of his suit scattered by the wind.
You: Shit.
Shyp: I had to leave him, you understand?! I didn’t want to! But what else could I have done?!
You: I don’t know, Shyp, I’m not here to judge you.
Shyp: I’m not judging myself, either. But now I have to live with it... for whatever time I have left.
sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerGP37OfferI_hint: Messages found on a dead loner's PDA
sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerGP37OfferI_body:
$J0L0You: Hey, bro. Word is, you’ve got a GP37?
Tikhon: I do. So what?
You: You selling?
Tikhon: Depends on the price.
You: I don’t have a ton of cash, but I have some interesting artifacts.
Tikhon: Yeah, but I can’t exactly shoot with artifacts, can I?
You: Listen, I propose a fair trade. I’ve got a Moonlight and a Thorn.
Tikhon: And what am I supposed to do with them?
You: Man, come on, they’re not duds! You wear them on your belt, or trade them to dealers for something rare.
Tikhon: So basically, I’d give up my good gun for a couple of shiny pebbles, right?
You: Bro, these are top-tier artifacts!
Tikhon: Great, but I need to shoot, not glow in the dark.
You: Alright, I can also add a Medusa.
Tikhon: Wow! And what would I do with three shiny rocks?
You: Sell them to the Barman! He also pays for them!
Tikhon: And get maybe half the GP37’s worth in the best case?
You: Well…
Tikhon: Let’s be honest, buddy. If you want this gun, either bring me something truly valuable or pay up in cash.
You: Fine, how about I throw in a Soul artifact too?
Tikhon: Oh, now that’s more interesting.
You: So? Deal??
Tikhon: Sure, if you also add a few packs of ammo. Maybe four mags of 5.45.
You: Ammo?!
Tikhon: Yeah. I’m giving you my main piece — I need some rounds for my backup. Ammo’s easier to get than a solid gun.
You: Damn it, alright.
Tikhon: Good. We’ll meet near the Bloodsucker Village at the campfire. I’ll message you the time later.
You: Got it, I’ll be in touch.
sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerExoOfferI_hint: Messages found on a dead loner's PDA
sid_notes_DSNoteRandLonerExoOfferI_body:
$J0L0You: Hey, old-timer! They say you’ve got an exo suit?
Borsuk: I do. So what?
You: Well, I was thinking... Maybe you’d sell it to me?
Borsuk: You fall off a tree, kid?
You: Why say that? I’m serious, I want decent gear for raids, and without an exo — you know how it is...
Borsuk: Do you even know what that thing is? Or do you think it’s just a fancy vest?
You: Heavy armor, enhances your legs, lets you carry more, offers solid protection. I’m not clueless.
Borsuk: Right. Plus the battery that’ll die on you, leaving you flailing like a turtle on its back.
You: It won’t die if I’m careful.
Borsuk: “Careful,” sure... Got money, “careful” boy?
You: Well, about that...
Borsuk: Thought so. No money, no brains.
You: Wait, it’s not that simple! I can give you some artifacts in exchange!
Borsuk: Why do all rookies think I’d trade an EXOSKELETON for a handful of glowing rocks?!
You: Not just random junk! I have a “Crystal,” a “Dummy,” and even a “Night Star”!
Borsuk: Kid, do you have any clue whatsoever?
You: Why?
Borsuk: Because your trinkets are shit compared to an exo. I wouldn’t even recoup 20% of its value.
You: But combined, they’re worth a lot!
Borsuk: Combined they’re worth maybe one-fifth of the exo’s price, you blockhead.
You: Maybe cut me a little slack for being a promising stalker?
Borsuk: You’ve barely done a single fucking raid. What’s so “promising” about you?
You: Soon I’ll make a name for myself, and you’ll be proud you helped a future legend!
Borsuk: Or you’ll become a legend as yet another corpse in a basement, thanks to a bloodsucker.
You: Come on, dude, please!

$J0L0You: Hey, Punktyr, you know a lot about Chornobyl’s history, right?
Punktyr: A bit, yeah. Why?

Punktyr: About the Nuclear Power Plant? Of course.
You: Not just the explosion, but the people who were there.
Punktyr: Plenty of stories, but one stuck with me the most.
You: Go on.
Punktyr: There was a team of firefighters from Pripyat who were called in the night of April 26, 1986. They had no protective gear, no real understanding of the situation. Just a call about a fire at the reactor.
You: These were the first to arrive?
Punktyr: Right. The group led by Lieutenant Volodymyr Pravik. They were told to extinguish the blaze, having no clue the core was exposed.
You: So what happened?
Punktyr: They went in. No radiation suits, no proper dosimeters, they were told “max 5 roentgen, no big deal.” In reality, it was hundreds of roentgen, lethal doses.
You: Damn...
Punktyr: They stood there dousing the burning graphite debris while they were basically soaking up massive radiation. Their bodies were already failing, but they had to keep going.
You: And then?
Punktyr: They all got taken to Hospital No. 6 a few days later.
You: Doctors tried to save them?
Punktyr: Yes, but they couldn’t. Their organs were shutting down, burned by radiation. They died one by one.
You: Fuuuck... And the lieutenant?
Punktyr: Pravik died first. The others followed days later. They were buried in sealed zinc coffins because even their bodies were radioactive.
You: That’s rough... They didn’t even know what they were sent into...
Punktyr: They didn’t. But they did their job. If not for them, the fire could have spread to other reactors.
You: That’s hardcore…
Punktyr: Next time some loudmouth says “it’s safe, no big deal,” remember those guys. One lie cost them life. The entire world was misled back then.
You: Yeah, I won’t forget this story.

If it had burned through to the bubbler pool below, where there was water, there would’ve been a SECOND explosion, powerful enough to wipe out not just the plant but half of Europe, creating a massive radioactive steam bomb.

You: And?

$J0L0Quantum: Hey, man, did you know the 1986 Chornobyl disaster could have stayed a secret?
You: Come on, who are you kidding? The explosion was massive, everyone noticed.
Quantum: True, but if not for Legasov and Shcherbina, the world might never have learned the full story.
You: Alright, you piqued my interest. Spill it.
Quantum: After the explosion, the USSR did the usual routine — hush it up. Classified documents, info control, telling locals everything was fine.
You: Nothing surprising there.
Quantum: But here’s the twist: two men wouldn’t let them bury the event. Valery Legasov, top nuclear physicist, and Boris Shcherbina, a Soviet official. They went to the site and saw it was far worse than reports claimed.
You: So what could they do?
Quantum: Legasov realized right away the reactor was basically destroyed, graphite out in the open, radiation levels off the charts. Shcherbina started off towing the party line, “no panic,” but Legasov convinced him otherwise.
You: So they tried to fix it, right?
Quantum: Yes. Shcherbina helped Legasov get the resources to contain the disaster as much as possible. But they both paid a price for telling the truth.
You: How so?
Quantum: Legasov found out the RBMK reactors had a design flaw: a positive void coefficient that caused the explosion. But Soviet officials wouldn’t admit it. When he went to the international conference in Vienna, he revealed more than the USSR wanted him to.
You: And they took him out?
Quantum: Eventually. They isolated him, discredited him, removed his name from papers. Ruined his career. Shcherbina also took heat, but he lived a few more years, dying in 1990, likely from complications of radiation.
You: And Legasov?
Quantum: April 26, 1988 — the second anniversary of the disaster. He ended his life. Left tapes detailing everything he knew. Only then did the Soviet regime admit the RBMK designs were flawed and started fixing them.
You: So he paid for the truth with his life?
Quantum: Yes. But without him, we might’ve had many more Chornobyls.
You: That’s quite a story...
Quantum: So next time some fuckface says “the truth is just words,” remember Legasov and Shcherbina, and the price they paid for it. And feel free to sock that dickhead in the jaw.

sid_notes_DSNoteKvashkaPast_body:
$J0L0Lately I’ve been haunted by strange dreams. Every night it’s the same: I stand on a riverbank whose water flows backward, returning to its source. On the opposite bank are silhouettes of people, their faces blurred, yet I feel I know them. They call out to me, but I can’t understand their words. I try to cross the river, but the water grows deeper, and I start to drown. I wake up feeling emptiness and loss.
These dreams leave me wondering: could they be echoes of my past? After all, I remember nothing of my life before I ended up here in the Zone. Other stalkers talk about their families, friends, who they were before. And me? I’m an empty shell with no memories, no roots.
Sometimes I catch myself trying to recall anything: a name, a face, a place. But it’s all a fog, just these dreams that won’t give me peace. Maybe this is punishment for something I’ve forgotten. Or maybe the Zone is toying with me, showing me things I never had.
Today, on guard duty, I found a child’s toy half-covered in dust. It seemed familiar, but I couldn’t remember why. That feeling of familiarity without memory tears me up inside. Who was I? Why am I here? Do I have anyone waiting for me outside the Zone?
Each new day brings more questions, but no answers. Only the dreams remain, a constant reminder I’ve lost something. But how do you lose what you can’t remember?
Maybe one day I’ll solve the puzzle of my existence. For now, I stay here in the darkness, trying to find some light among the shadows of my mind. At least I have the brothers who always support me. They’re my only family.

P.S. The quartermaster said he’d swap my old PDA for a new one, so this is probably my last entry here. This device is all I have left of my past. But they say letting go is the hardest part, so I guess I’ll just have to find the strength to turn the page.

$J0L0Marker: Hey, friend. If I can still call you that... How’s it going? Never thought we’d end up on opposite sides of the barricade.
You: Hey, Marker. Well, “barricade” might be a strong word. I just stand for living freely in the Zone without draconian restrictions, and you stand for your “Duty,” wanting to destroy it.
Marker: Surprising to me, since you used to say the Zone was a curse, that there’s nothing here but deadly danger. What changed? A couple shiny artifacts got in your head?
You: My outlook changed when I realized the Zone isn’t just horror, it’s a phenomenon to be studied and utilized. “Freedom” isn’t about blindly razing or fencing everything off.
Marker: We’ll see how that holds up when anomalies kill more people and mutants creep beyond the Zone. “Duty” stands for safety. We prefer discipline and order, not chaotic “research.”
You: You call it chaos. We do have order, just not your militaristic style. We don’t force people to follow orders; we have our own code.
Marker: That code basically seems like “do whatever.” I’ve seen your boys handle issues with violence just like any bandits.
You: Don’t lump us in with bandits. “Freedom” values free will, but not baseless brutality. And if one of ours did cross that line, well, every group has bad eggs, right?
Marker: Yeah, but bad eggs ruin your rep. From the outside, it looks like each of you is your own commander. With “Duty,” that doesn’t happen; we have a clear hierarchy. Everyone knows their job when things get tough.
You: Great if you’re in a war. But the Zone isn’t just a fucking battlefield. It has its own laws; you coexist with it, not constantly douse the fire with gasoline.
Marker: We’ll see where you run when things really heat up. Maybe you’ll come crawling for the protection of the “militarists.”
You: Don’t worry, if it gets hot, we can handle ourselves. “Freedom” isn’t defenseless, you know. Remember the Barrier? Hell, we went there together once.
Marker: Yeah, so we did. Alright, in the meantime, we each do our job. But if your approach leads to more chaos, we’ll step in.
You: Got it. Also remember the Zone isn’t so easily “cleansed” or conquered. It might well turn on you.
Marker: Amen, brother. Can’t deny that. Maybe one day we’ll think back to when we just stalked together, no banners. But seems those days are gone.
You: Time moves on. Take care, Marker, and don’t end up in our crosshairs.
Marker: If fate brings us together, I won’t shoot first, I promise. But don’t see it as an invitation to buddy up. Stay safe.

$J0L0So, it's time to pay your debts, scum. Did you think everyone forgot what you did a few years ago? Every other stalker here is sharpening a knife for you. All we dream about is seeing every last one of you die in anomalies. And if not there, we'll finish the job ourselves.

And you can tell your boss this: those who plan to take the Zone and all free people under their control will, in the end, only take it up the ass.
sid_notes_DSNoteDesolation_body:
$J0L0Funny how things turn out. For so long, I lived on the Big Land, peddling Zone trinkets, earning whatever I could. But even in the most hopeless situation, I never thought of coming to this cursed place.
And here I am. Life has a very peculiar sense of humor. This place brings nothing but despair and a feeling of desolation. As if my very mind—along with all my dreams and plans—became just as dead and covered in dust as the buildings in that so-called ghost town.

$J0L0Mysterious Explosions in Residential Buildings: A Journalistic Investigation
Recently, a series of mysterious explosions occurred in residential apartments in several Ukrainian cities, causing panic among the population and attracting the attention of law enforcement agencies. A journalist from our newspaper decided to conduct his own investigation to determine the possible causes of these incidents.
The first incident took place in Kharkiv, where an explosion destroyed an apartment on the third floor of a multi-story building. Fortunately, the residents were away, and no one was injured. Similar incidents occurred in Odesa and Dnipro, where explosions also took place in vacant apartments, making it more difficult to find witnesses and establish the causes.
Officials have not yet provided detailed comments, citing the confidentiality of the investigation. However, according to unofficial information, the theories under consideration range from household gas leaks to intentional arson. The most intriguing theory, though, involves an anomalous aspect. Some experts note a possible connection to the activities of the Chernobyl Anomalous Zone Research Institute (NDIICHAZ), given its research in energy and physics.
Our journalist reached out to NDIICHAZ representatives for comment. In response, the institute’s press service stated that its activities are strictly regulated and that no experiments that could lead to such incidents have been conducted. Nevertheless, given the classified nature of many studies, the public continues to express concern.
Local residents are organizing community meetings, demanding transparency from the authorities and a prompt investigation. Psychologists report a rise in anxiety levels among the population, which could lead to social instability if the situation is not resolved soon.
We will continue to monitor developments and keep our readers informed of new details regarding this mysterious and alarming phenomenon.

$J0L0SCIENTIFIC REPORT
"PHYSICOCHEMICAL AND BIOLOGICAL ASPECTS OF THE STUDY OF THE HOOF OF THE MUTATED BOAR (SUS SCROFA ANOMALUS) IN THE CONTEXT OF ITS POSSIBLE PHARMACOLOGICAL APPLICATION"
Authors: Anton Nehoda, Yevhen Osachka
Laboratory of Experimental Biochemistry of Anomalous Objects, Institute of Applied Biophysics, Exclusion Zone

ABSTRACT
As a result of biological monitoring of newly mutated organisms within the Exclusion Zone, a number of morphophysiological changes have been identified in representatives of the class Mammalia. One of the most interesting objects of the research became the mutated boar (Sus scrofa anomalus), whose biochemical composition attracted attention due to its abnormal regenerative capacity and increased structural stability of connective tissues. In particular, the hoof tissue of this organism has demonstrated a unique combination of organo-mineral compounds that can theoretically be applied in the development of new pharmacological drugs.

INTRODUCTION
Anomalous mutagenic processes induced by high levels of ionizing radiation and gravitational fluctuations within the Zone lead to the emergence of new biological structures with atypical chemical and physical properties.
Preliminary analysis of tissue samples from mutated animals revealed:
- Fibrillar proteins with an increased level of molecular ordering.
- Polymeric inclusions based on silicon radicals of unknown origin.
- Presence of piezoactive structures within keratin formations.
The purpose of this study is to identify bioactive compounds in the hoof of the mutated boar and assess their potential application in pharmacology.

MATERIALS AND METHODS
1. Sample collection
Hoof material was obtained from specimens found in sector R-13, on the edge of the “Deposits” zone (coordinates hidden). The sampling was carried out by cryopreservation (t=-78.5°C), transportation in an inert gas environment.
2. Physicochemical analysis
- Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) – identification of organic compounds.
- Raman spectroscopy – analysis of structural changes in proteins.
- Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) – study of molecular composition.
- Electron microscopy (SEM and TEM) – analysis of the supramolecular organization of hoof material.
3. Biological tests
The extract of the mutated boar’s hoof was studied on:
- Human epithelial cell cultures (HaCaT) – assessment of regenerative activity.
- Model organisms (Mus musculus, BALB/c strain) – analysis of wound healing rates.
- Modified blood plasma samples – study of coagulation properties.

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
1. Chemical composition
The presence of hyperstable keratin containing modified disulfide bonds and abnormal metal-organic inclusions was identified.
Identified compounds:
- N-methylthioproline – a potential regulator of tissue regeneration.
- Polysiloxane complexes – structural analogs of biological silica.
- Organic polymeric nanofibrils of unknown origin that do not degrade in acidic or alkaline environments.
2. Biological activity
- The growth of HaCaT culture in the presence of the extract increased by 312% (p<0.01), indicating a powerful regenerative effect.
- In model animals, the wound healing time was reduced by 2.8 times, surpassing the effectiveness of known healing agents.
- Hemostatic effect – the extract significantly accelerated blood clotting without signs of thrombosis.

CONCLUSIONS
1. The hoof tissue of the mutated boar contains a number of unique compounds with potential biomedical properties.
2. The discovered regenerative and hemostatic effect may have practical application in military medicine and in experimental programs for human adaptation to Zone conditions.
3. Further research should be aimed at identifying the molecular mechanisms of action of the active components and their safety for humans.

WARNING
The obtained results indicate a potentially high biological risk of uncontrolled use of bioactive extracts from mutated organisms. Further toxicological studies are required before any clinical trials.
